record.paper_title: The Volume of Vector Fields on Riemannian Manifolds: Main Results and Open Problems
record.original_question: Let a finite subgroup G of U(m+1) act freely by isometries on the Berger sphere (S^{2m+1}, g_mu), and let H_mu^G be the induced unit Hopf vector field on the quotient S^{2m+1}/G. Determine the values of mu, depending on G and m, for which H_mu^G is stable, including the open case of projective spaces with m odd.

evidence.quote: The stability problem is still open in general
find the values of .μG for which .HμG is stable

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For an integer m ≥ 1 and a parameter μ > 0, let the Berger sphere be the odd-dimensional sphere S^{2m+1} ⊂ C^{m+1} equipped with the one-parameter family of Riemannian metrics g_μ obtained from the round metric g_1 by rescaling lengths in the direction of the standard Hopf vector field by the factor μ; explicitly, if V is the unit Hopf vector field (Vp = i p for p ∈ S^{2m+1}) and H is its orthogonal complement in T S^{2m+1}, then g_μ = μ^2 g_1|_{V} ⊕ g_1|_{H}. The vector field H_μ := (1/μ) V is then a unit vector field on (S^{2m+1}, g_μ).

Let G be a finite subgroup of U(m+1) acting freely by isometries on (S^{2m+1}, g_μ); the action descends to the quotient M_μ^G := S^{2m+1}/G, on which H_μ induces a well-defined unit vector field H_μ^G. Consider the volume functional
   F(X) = ∫_{M_μ^G} √det(Id + (∇X)^t ∇X) dvol_{g_μ}
defined on the space of smooth unit vector fields X on (M_μ^G, g_μ); the unit Hopf vector field H_μ^G is a critical point of F.

Problem: Determine, in terms of G and m, the precise set of values μ > 0 for which H_μ^G is a stable critical point of the volume functional F (i.e. the Hessian of F at H_μ^G is positive semidefinite on the tangent space to the unit vector field constraint). In particular, settle the case of the real and complex projective space quotients with m odd.
artifact.category_tag: Stability of unit vector fields on Riemannian manifolds
artifact.status_search_result: Partial results are known: for 0 < μ ≤ 1, H_μ^G is stable for volume (and energy) on quotients S^{2m+1}/G with m ≥ 1, and for Berger real projective spaces RP^{4m-1} the threshold μ = 1 is sharp (instability for μ > 1). However, the full classification of stability values μ depending on G and m remains open in general, including the projective space case with m odd, as indicated by the cited literature on stability of unit Hopf vector fields on quotients of Berger spheres.

status_evidence.title: Stability of unit Hopf vector fields on quotients of spheres
status_evidence.snippet: For 0 < μ ≤ 1, H_μ^Γ is stable for energy and volume; sharp on Berger projective spaces RP^{4m-1}.
status_evidence.claim: Partial stability results known; cannot be improved on certain projective quotients.

status_evidence.title: Unit vector fields of minimum energy on quotients of spheres and stability of the Reeb vector field
status_evidence.snippet: Further results on stability of Reeb/Hopf fields on quotients of Berger spheres.
status_evidence.claim: Topic remains under active investigation with open subcases.
